zhnsuSnMELM.text: Why do thousands of random iron particles suddenly arrange themselves into beautiful curved patterns around a magnet? You might think the magnet is simply pulling them into invisible lines, but something much more interesting is happening. Iron is ferromagnetic. When exposed to a magnetic field, its internal magnetic domains reorganize, turning each tiny filing into a temporary magnet. Every single grain is doing this all at once.
